summary: J. S. Pade was an Indologist. He held posts as a Research Officer at the University of Chicago (attested 1963) and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1966).

J. Thomas Rimer is a scholar of Japanology who studied at Princeton University and Columbia University. He held positions at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of Maryland, College Park (~1986–2004), UCLA, and the University of Pittsburgh (~1990–2010).
J.-M. Grandjean was a linguist who studied at the University of Lyon under Paul Regnaud.

Jaan Puhvel was a linguist and Indologist who studied at McGill, Uppsala, Harvard, and UC Berkeley, working under Joshua Whatmough, Georges Dumézil, and Stig Wikander. He held an academic post at the University of California, Berkeley.

Jabez Cornelius Whitley was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his B.A. at Queens' College (1855–1859) and served as a missionary for the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts beginning in 1862.

Jack Goody was a historian, archaeologist, and religious studies scholar who studied at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1946). He later served as a retired professor at the University of Cambridge from ~1984 to 2015.

Jack Kornfield is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Dartmouth and Saybrook, learning under Ajahn Chah, Wing-tsit Chan, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma. He co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Spirit Rock Meditation Center.
Jack Laughlin is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999 and held an academic post at the University of Sudbury.
Jacob Antoon van Velze was an Indologist. He studied at Utrecht University under Willem Caland and Jan Gonda, earning his Ph.D. in 1938.

Jacob Ensink was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and Frederik David Kan Bosch. He served as Lecturer of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1954 to 1962.

Jacob Fisher is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2021–2025). He has held teaching and administrative posts at Oxford, Nalanda Monastery, and Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Jacob Grimm was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Marburg (~1802–1806). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, studying under Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).

Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He has held academic posts at the College of William & Mary as Assistant Professor of Religion and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob Neusner was a religious studies scholar educated at Harvard, Lincoln College, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary. He held posts at UW–Milwaukee, Brandeis, the University of South Florida (~1990–2000), and Bard College (~2000–2014).

Jacob P. Dalton is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Idaho, UC Davis, and Michigan. He held posts at the British Library, SOAS, Yale (2005), and UC Berkeley (attested 2011–2026).

Jacob Samuel Speyer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University. He served as Lektor at the University of Amsterdam, Professor at the University of Groningen, and Professor at Leiden University.

Jacob Wackernagel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Basel, Göttingen, and Leipzig. He was a professor at the University of Basel (1879–1902, 1915–1936) and held the chair of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).
Jacobus Arntz was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He taught philosophy, philology, and natural sciences at Kuilenburg Seminary (1843–1847, 1862–1865) and at the Major Seminary of Roermond.
Jacobus Marinus van der Hoogt was an Indologist who studied at the University of Amsterdam, earning his Ph.D. under the supervision of Barend Faddegon in 1929.
